agentSetup.heading: Agent setup
agentSetup.description: Create a token and configure it in your Agent's secure environment, then give the Agent the setup instructions.
agentSetup.loopbackHint: This is a local address. Remote Agents need a server address they can reach.
agentSetup.notifyClipboardFailedDescription: Copy the setup instructions below manually.
agentSetup.instructions:
Please use Drill Hub to help me plan my learning, create learning content and practice, and review learning results as needed.

Public server address: {baseUrl}
API base address: {apiBase}
Authentication: Authorization: Bearer {'<'}AGENT_TOKEN{'>'}. Read the actual token from the DRILL_HUB_AGENT_TOKEN environment variable in your secure configuration. Do not ask me for my password or echo the token in conversations, logs or learning materials.

First download and extract the Skill from {skillUrl}, read drill-hub/SKILL.md and references/api.md, then call GET {capabilityUrl} to confirm token permissions and supported capabilities. Do not guess undocumented endpoints.
Create resources in dependency order: topic -> content/questions -> practice or exam -> plan tasks. Use the actual IDs and revisions from responses. Content currently supports plain text only.
Internal model questions are graded by the server using a rubric. Only submit per-criterion levels and verbatim evidence for external_rubric questions when the token has grade:write permission. Never specify scores directly.
Read results as needed, without frequent polling. On update conflicts, read the resource again first. If a creation request has an uncertain result, check existing resources rather than retrying blindly. Use archive and restore by default; do not permanently delete resources.

gradeFeedback.pendingDescription: Answers are locked. Pending grading does not count as zero points.
gradeFeedback.failedDescription: This is not a zero score. Any existing valid grade is preserved. Check the report again later.

questionNav.title: Questions
questionNav.descriptionReview: Green means correct, red means incorrect. Unanswered and ungraded questions stay neutral.
questionNav.descriptionMarked: Green means answered; pale yellow means partially answered. An amber border marks the current question, a check mark means locked, and a triangle in the top-right corner means marked.
questionNav.descriptionPlain: Green means answered; pale yellow means partially answered. An amber border marks the current question, and a check mark means locked.
